source_snapshot.title: fix(php): resolve imports by namespace
source_snapshot.body:
Fixes #441

## Summary

Resolve explicit PHP type imports by their declared namespace instead of a repository-wide short-name match.

## Type
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Test
- [ ] CI

## Changes
- Preserve semicolon, braced, and global PHP namespace scope on parsed type entities.
- Build case-insensitive fully qualified indexes for PHP classes, interfaces, traits, and enums across batches.
- Resolve explicit type imports through their exact fully qualified name without changing function and constant import behavior.
- Distinguish constructor, function, member, and static calls through edge resolution and patch construction.
- Leave aliased and grouped PHP import parsing outside this change.

## Validation

- Focused PHP parser and resolution tests: 103 passed, 1 skipped.
- Ix CLI tests: 928 passed, 1 skipped, including parser smoke tests.
- Typecheck, build, lint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The unrelated core baseline still has six pre-existing failures involving unavailable fixtures and existing snapshots.

## Checklist
- [x] Tests pass
- [x] Smoke tests pass
- [x] No raw errors introduced
- [x] CLI output follows Ix format

## Release checklist (if merging to main)
- [ ] `ix-cli/package.json` version bumped
- [ ] After merge: tag pushed (`git tag vX.Y.Z && git push origin vX.Y.Z`)
- [ ] If backend changes: `ix-memory-layer` tagged and released first
- [ ] If `docker-compose.standalone.yml` changed: verified `curl | sh` install works

comments.body:
Reviewed. The FQCN indexing is a real improvement and the `trimPhpNamespace` rewrite in `83079ff` correctly kills the flagged ReDoS — that CodeQL alert is **stale** and can be dismissed after a re-scan.

Blocking issue: widening the capture to `[(qualified_name) (name)]` also captures the alias, because in `namespace_use_clause` the alias is a direct `(name)` sibling. `use Vendor[local-path]\User as Admin;` therefore emits an `IMPORTS` edge to an unrelated `Admin` class the file never imports, and promotes the wrong short-name matches from 0.5 to **0.9** — the opposite of what this PR is for.

Two related clause-scoping bugs: `importAliased` is computed from the whole statement, so one alias in a comma-separated `use` disables FQCN resolution for every clause; and that same unanchored `/[local-path]\s+/` is a second instance of the ReDoS class CodeQL missed (~3.7s on a `use` padded with 100k spaces, which is valid PHP).

All three fixed by one root-cause change — scope to the clause: **Hiro-Chiba/Ix#3**.

Added a second commit to **Hiro-Chiba/Ix#3** covering two further regressions I measured against main rather than inferred:

**1. A `use` leaks across braced namespace blocks.** `phpFqcnImportsByLocal` is keyed by file, but a `use` is scoped to its namespace block:

```php
namespace A { use Vendor[local-path]\Thing; function run(Thing $t) {...} }
namespace B { class Thing {} function go(Thing $t) {...} }
```

`go()` resolved to `Vendor/Package/Thing.php` at 0.9 although `B` declares its own `Thing` two lines up. main emits no edge for `go` at all. One namespace per file is the PSR-12 norm, so the index now skips a multi-block file rather than mis-resolve it — restoring main's behaviour exactly for that shape.

**2. Duplicate CALLS edges reach the graph.** `phpCallKind` splits the per-file dedup key, so `log()` and `Logger::log()` survive as two relationships. When both resolve to the same member, patch-builder salts the edge id by call kind and emits two `UpsertEdge` ops with identical `src`/`dst`/`predicate` but different ids — and the dedup downstream keys on id, so both commit. Measured: main 1 op, this branch 2. The salt still applies when the two kinds resolve to *different* nodes, which is what it's for.

Update on how this lands: **#446** now carries your commits plus the review fixes, targeting `main` directly. It's up for review by @josephismikhail.

No action needed from you. Your commits keep their authorship on that branch, and it will be merged with a merge commit rather than a squash so that stays true — when it lands, this PR closes as *merged*. The follow-up PR I'd opened into your fork is closed as superseded.

The reasoning for each fix is in this thread above and in #446's description.
